newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes flat in Asia, W. African cargoes bought.
newsitem.headline: Crudes flat in Asia, W. African cargoes bought.

text.p: Crude oil prices were mostly unchanged in Asia on Friday with the market quiet in the absence of many traders in the region due to a public holiday, market participants said.
Physical trading was mostly quiet with reports of West African deals believed done recently dominating the market.

June cash Brent was notionally assessed at about $17.70/17.80 per barrel, virtually unchanged from late U.S. trading levels. Brent spreads were assessed at levels similar to the late U.S. market, with May/June assessed at minus 32 to minus 29 and June/July at minus 22 to minus 19.
In Brent/Dubai spreads, June was assessed at $1.30/1.36, virtually unchanged from late U.S. trading while July was assessed at $1.40/1.45, compared with $1.45/1.50.
There were no fresh reports of wet deals done for June Gulf crudes, traders said.
However, a spate of West African crudes are believed to have been done recently on the back of softer Brent prices, traders said.
Some Chinese, South Korean and Japanese companies are believed to have taken advantage of the widening arbitrage window and bought West African crudes.
A Japanese trader said it had sold a late May Palanca at dated Brent plus 11 cents, but declined to provide a name for the buyer or the destination.
Elsewhere a Japanese oil refiner was believed to have purchased a West African crude, but details were unavailable.
The purchase of West African cargoes was expected to sap requirements for some June-loading Gulf crudes, most notably Oman, some traders said.
